title: B. C. 30,000
summary: "B. C. 30,000" by S. P. Meek is a novel written in the early 20th century that presents a fictional account of prehistoric life, focusing on the conflicts between early humans and Neanderthal-like creatures. The story unfolds against the backdrop of the dawn of civilization, capturing the struggles for survival, power dynamics within tribes, and the challenges posed by rival factions in an ancient world. The narrative follows Anak the Hunter, a Cro-Magnon man, as he navigates tribal leadership, romantic desire, and the constant threats from Neanderthal competitors. Tensions escalate as rivalries surface, leading to a fight for authority and survival that challenges the structure of their tribe. When the Neanderthalers abduct Una, Anak, alongside his loyal friend Invar, embarks on a perilous quest to rescue her, ultimately culminating in a climactic battle that tests their strength and cunning against both their human adversaries and the primitive dangers of their world.
